title: Maase Inc. and Galaxyeye Form Strategic Partnership to Build Embodied AI Home Ecosystem
summary: Maase Inc. (NASDAQ: MAAS) today officially announced that its subsidiary, Huazhi Future, has signed a strategic partnership agreement with H
body_text: Maase Inc. (NASDAQ: MAAS) today officially announced that its subsidiary, Huazhi Future, has signed a strategic partnership agreement with Hangzhou Galaxyeye Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Galaxyeye"). The two parties will engage in deep collaboration across embodied AI cognitive systems, home-focused vertical applications, and industry ecosystem integration, with the goal of jointly building an embodied AI ecosystem and accelerating the innovative adoption and commercialization of these technologies in Chinese household environments. Currently, with the significant growth in demand for home-based elderly care and the rapid rise of the "silver economy," the home scenario has emerged as one of the most promising directions for the deployment of artificial intelligence technology. Market demand is steadily rising for intelligent agents capable of emotional interaction, long-term memory, proactive safeguarding, and companionship. As the next major frontier in artificial intelligence, embodied AI is accelerating its expansion into home life scenarios. Against this industry backdrop, Maase Inc.'s subsidiary, Huazhi Future, is comprehensively accelerating its strategic footprint in embodied AI for home scenarios, having launched the robot brain ecological product, LUMI, in April this year. The product primarily focuses on key areas such as home monitoring, emergency communication safeguarding, intelligent companionship for the elderly, health management services, and long-term household memory systems. In May, LUMI successfully debuted at the 8th Western China International Fair for Investment and Trade (WCIFIT), delivering an exceptional live interactive experience to numerous attending guests, media representatives, and visitors. The partnership between Huazhi Future and Galaxyeye will greatly facilitate the complementary strengths of both parties across the upstream and downstream of the industry chain. Since its founding in 2015 by AI scientist Dr. Qian Xiaoyi, Galaxyeye has been dedicated to the research and development of human-like AI technologies. The company boasts core capabilities including its proprietary "One Brain, Multiple Forms" architecture, decoupled cognitive systems, and general long-term memory infrastructure. Meanwhile, Huazhi Future remains deeply focused on building the application system for embodied AI in home scenarios, continuously upgrading its relevant product and service capabilities. According to the strategic partnership agreement, the two parties will engage in deep synergy across the following four core areas: ● Technological Breakthroughs and Iteration: Centered on the real-world scenarios of Chinese home safeguarding, the two parties will conduct joint adaptation and in-depth optimization of the general-purpose brain capabilities of embodied AI, driving continuous iterative upgrades of core competencies based on user scenario demands. ● Industry Chain Product Co-creation: Uniting upstream and downstream industry chain ecosystem partners in power modules, sensing hardware, and computing networks, both parties will jointly construct a comprehensive home safeguarding ecosystem, promoting efficient synergy within the embodied AI industry chain. ● Industry Standard Formulation: Focusing on the practical application of embodied AI in home scenarios, the partners will actively participate in the research and formulation of relevant industry standards, guiding and fostering the standardized development of the industry. ● Brand and Ecosystem Building: Through diversified formats such as industry summits, technology forums, and joint press conferences, the two parties will comprehensively showcase their ecosystem development achievements, continuously expanding industry synergistic effects and brand influence. This partnership with Galaxyeye is expected to further enhance LUMI’s core capabilities and ecosystem integration for home applications, accelerating the real-world deployment of embodied AI technologies in household environments. Looking ahead, Maase Inc. will continue expanding its strategic presence across intelligent computing infrastructure, vertical AI applications, and embodied AI, while collaborating with additional ecosystem partners to advance the next generation of home intelligence.

title: Malloc LTD Selected for the Prestigious European Defence Innovation Scheme (EUDIS) Business…
body_text: Malloc LTD Selected for the Prestigious European Defence Innovation Scheme (EUDIS) Business Accelerator Cohort #3 Maria Terzi 2 min read · Jul 6, 2026 -- Press enter or click to view image in full size Malloc LTD Selected for the Prestigious European Defence Innovation Scheme (EUDIS) Business Accelerator Cohort #3 NICOSIA, CYPRUS — July 2026 Malloc LTD, an AI-driven mobile cybersecurity company specializing in advanced spyware blocking and secure communications, today announced its selection into Cohort #3 of the European Defence Innovation Scheme (EUDIS) Business Accelerator. Out of a record-breaking 499 applications from across the European Union and Norway, Malloc is one of only 20 high-potential companies chosen to participate in this highly competitive, eight-month program. Initiated by the European Commission and the European Defence Agency, the EUDIS Business Accelerator is designed to bolster Europe’s sovereign defense and dual-use technological base by fast-tracking breakthrough commercial innovations into the defense sector. Get Maria Terzi’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Remember me for faster sign in The program, which officially kicks off in September 2026, provides selected scale-ups with intensive, tailored commercial coaching, direct mentorship from defense industry specialists, and access to advanced technical testing facilities. Over the next eight months, Malloc will participate in five immersive, regional bootcamps across Europe, connecting directly with defense leaders, end-users, and specialized institutional investors. Upon successful completion of the milestones, Malloc will also receive a €120,000 seed-funding voucher to further accelerate its dual-use product trajectory. “Securing a spot in Cohort #3 out of nearly 500 applicants is a powerful validation of Malloc’s core technology,” said Maria Terzi, CEO of Malloc. “Advanced spyware blocking and completely secure mobile communications are no longer just corporate necessities — they are critical requirements for modern defense infrastructure. Through the EUDIS framework, we look forward to adapting our AI-driven privacy solutions to meet the rigorous demands of the European defense ecosystem and contributing to a safer, more resilient Europe.” Malloc’s inclusion highlights the growing urgency for intelligent mobile defense software capable of intercepting sophisticated, zero-day spyware threats and safeguarding sensitive data channels in real time. About Malloc LTD Malloc LTD is an AI-driven mobile cybersecurity company specializing in spyware blocking and secure communications. Utilizing proprietary, on-device machine learning models, Malloc monitors mobile environments to detect and block unauthorized surveillance, prevent spyware execution, and encrypt communication channels in real time. Malloc helps individual users and enterprises worldwide protect their data and safeguard sensitive mobile intelligence. Learn more at mallocprivacy.com . About the EUDIS Business Accelerator The European Defence Innovation Scheme (EUDIS) Business Accelerator is a landmark initiative powered by the European Defence Fund (EDF). Implemented alongside major European defense ecosystems and industrial partners like Starburst Aero, the program aims to close the gap between commercial tech innovators and European defense requirements, providing up to 20 exceptional companies per cohort with funding, elite mentoring, and strategic go-to-market channels. body_text: View All News TOYO Appoints Yasunari Harada as Chief Financial Officer and Director July 1, 2026 TOKYO , July 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TOYO Co., Ltd (Nasdaq: TOYO) (OTC: TOYWF), ("TOYO" or the "Company"), a solar manufacturing company, today announced the appointment of Yasunari Harada as Chief Financial Officer and a director of the Company, effective July 1. Mr. Harada, a seasoned executive with over 30 years of senior leadership at leading investment banks, will play a central role in strengthening the Company's financial strategy, investor relations and capital markets engagement. Mr. Harada is replacing Taewoo "Raymond" Chung, who resigned as Chief Financial Officer and a director, effective June 30, 2026. Mr. Harada's career spans some of the most respected institutions in global finance. He began at The Industrial Bank of Japan before holding senior roles as Vice President at Morgan Stanley Securities, Executive Director at BNP Paribas Securities, and Managing Director & Head of Financial Institutions at Société Générale Securities in Tokyo. He has served on the boards of financial institutions across Asia and Central Asia, including Kyrgyzkommertsbank, Solid Bank, and Khan Bank. Mr. Harada holds a bachelor of law degree from Kyushu University and is fluent in Japanese and English. "Yasunari's appointment marks a defining moment for TOYO," said Mr. Takahiko Onozuka, Chief Executive Officer. "His extensive experience will be instrumental as we refine our financial strategy, deepen our engagement with the investment community, and expand our institutional footprint. We also extend our sincere gratitude to Mr. Chung for his dedicated service to TOYO, and wish him every success in his future endeavors." Mr. Harada's appointment strengthens a leadership team already positioned for the next phase, bringing world-class financial discipline, cross-border capital markets access, and the credibility of a career built at globally recognized institutions. "TOYO has a strong foundation, and I am dedicated to helping drive our growth," said Mr. Harada. "I look forward to working closely with Mr. Onozuka and the entire team to build shareholder value, strengthen our financial position, and demonstrate TOYO's potential to the global investment community." About TOYO Co., Ltd. TOYO is a solar manufacturing company that is committed to becoming a vertically integrated solar manufacturer in the global market, integrating the upstream production of wafers and silicon, midstream production of solar cells, downstream production of photovoltaic modules, and potentially other stages of the solar power supply chain. TOYO is well-positioned to produce high-quality solar cells and modules at a competitive scale and cost. title: Humanizing AI CX with Luxury Strategies
summary: Humanizing AI CX with Luxury Strategies
body_text: Harnessing high-end luxury service principles with cutting-edge customer experience (CX) technology defines Sophi Conti’s career. In a highly informative episode of PL-ai-N Speak, I had the pleasure of hosting Sophie to discuss her insider viewpoints as the founder of Customer Service (CS) Lab — which is a leading consultancy that helps teams from top companies like Etsy, Mailchimp, and more stay on CX’s cutting edge. Our conversation underscores the importance of harmonizing AI to enhance CS’s human aspects, ensuring a balance between efficiency and personalized care. For the growth-stage companies that CS Lab supports, this means not only adopting AI and technological tools but also nurturing a team culture that values empathy, attention to detail, and a deep understanding of customer needs. Sophie's insights provide a roadmap for CX leaders to navigate various complexities to integrate AI into their customer support strategies — all without losing sight of the human touch that defines exceptional service. CX’s Transformation Era Sophie notes a transformative era in customer experience, propelled by two main factors that she sees in her consultancy: generative AI’s meteoric rise and the post-pandemic economic realities. Generative AI promises a significant boost in CX productivity, allowing companies to navigate budget constraints and workforce changes. This transformation challenges CX leaders to integrate AI seamlessly into their processes without losing the human touch that remains critical in building customer relationships. Navigating Challenges: Team Cohesion and AI Integration Sophie emphasizes how important it is to maintain team cohesion and align with brand values — despite economic pressures and high turnover rates. Foundational training focusing on soft skills, aligned with company core values, is vital in preserving a cohesive team culture. Moreover, developing and integrating an AI strategy requires a clear understanding of goals, whether it's enhancing agent productivity or improving customer self-service. Selecting AI solutions that support seamless integration and preparing the human team for this digital transformation are crucial steps. Then, as the boundaries between support, success, and sales begin to blur, upskilling CS agents in these domains will empower individuals even more. This preparation is essential for navigating the more complex and nuanced issues that AI will leave for human agents to handle. CS Future: Anticipatory and Personalized Looking ahead, Sophie envisions a customer support landscape where AI not only boosts productivity but also enables a seamless, anticipatory experience. The future of CX lies in leveraging AI to gain real-time insights into customer journeys. This ensures personalized service by leveraging proactive support. In this new world. Sophie believes human agents will become even more critical, where they can now hyper-focus on building relationships and delivering memorable experiences that tie customers to brands.

title: 64x Bio Launches AAV Apex Suite to Power the Next Generation of Gene Therapy Manufacturing
body_text: Five global biopharma and CDMO leaders have entered strategic collaborations for AAV Apex Suite. High performance product line built on 64x Bio’s VectorSelect platform, delivering titers exceeding E15 vg/L. ‍ ‍ SAN FRANCISCO – 64x Bio , a biotech company developing scalable solutions for the production of advanced therapies, today announced the launch of AAV Apex Suite, a high yield product line designed to meet one of the most urgent bottlenecks in gene therapy — manufacturing. ‍ Gene therapies have the potential to cure diseases but there are significant barriers preventing many of these transformational medicines from reaching patients. High cost of goods and limited manufacturing scale have restricted its use to a select number of therapeutic indications. AAV Apex Suite represents a major step in addressing these challenges, enabling partners to achieve top tier titers. AAV Apex Suite includes suspension-adapted HEK293 cell lines for transient transfection alongside optimized production processes that consistently deliver titers exceeding E15 vg/L. Product performance has been independently confirmed by partners across a range of serotypes and therapeutic payloads, at high titer and quality. ‍ "The grand challenges for gene therapies have shifted from target organ specificity and how to fit large genes into small capsids to the challenge of low-cost, high-quality manufacturing of AAV therapies. So it is with great pleasure that we see this milestone from 64x," said George Church, PhD, Co-founder of 64x Bio. ‍ AAV Apex Suite demonstrates the power of 64x Bio’s VectorSelect platform, housing a massive and expanding map of data that uncovers cellular programs driving yield. VectorSelect reveals both genetic and metabolic insights that inform cell line engineering and nutrient formulations for media components, to maximize productivity. As VectorSelect’s cell map continues to grow, 64x Bio is increasingly able to apply computational tools to refine its platform to accelerate the design of future products. ‍ “Our goal is to enable gene therapies and next generation medicines to succeed by fixing the cost and scale problems that hold them back,” said Lexi Rovner, PhD, CEO and Co-founder of 64x Bio. “Our team has done incredible work to develop AAV Apex Suite as an initial demonstration of what our platform can achieve. We’re already building on this foundation and continuing to develop more that we’ll be sharing soon,” she added. ‍ Five leading global biopharma and CDMOs have already entered strategic collaborations to evaluate AAV Apex Suite, reflecting growing urgency to overcome manufacturing bottlenecks threatening the future of gene therapy. While AAV Apex Suite currently supports transient production, stable cell lines are in development — the suite will continue to expand in this way, with tools for AAV. VectorSelect has broader applications and 64x Bio is actively exploring future expansion into advanced biologics outside of AAV. Beyond off-the-shelf offerings through AAV Apex Suite, 64x Bio partners with developers to engineer custom solutions through VectorSelect and is rapidly expanding access to both. ‍ To learn more about AAV Apex Suite and explore collaboration opportunities using 64x Bio’s VectorSelect platform, visit www.64xbio.com . ‍ Contacts Kimberly Ha KKH Advisors 917-291-5744 kimberly.ha@kkhadvisors.com ‍ Lexi Rovner 64x Bio info@64xbio.com

title: Comprehensive B2B SaaS Benchmarks for 2026
summary: Discover key B2B SaaS benchmarks for 2026, including CAC, NRR, and Growth Rates.
body_text: TL;DR: Key B2B SaaS benchmarks include CAC, NRR, ACV, and their implications for strategic planning. Comprehensive B2B SaaS Benchmarks for 2026 Last updated: July 2026 The economic landscape is evolving, influencing B2B SaaS metrics and benchmarks. As companies seek more strategic insights, understanding these metrics offers an avenue for optimized decision-making in 2026. What Are the Key B2B SaaS Benchmarks for 2026? Understanding B2B SaaS benchmarks is crucial for evaluating company health and planning for growth. Key metrics. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), Net Revenue Retention (NRR), and Annual Contract Value (ACV). Offer insights into efficiency and sustainability. The goal is not only to understand these figures but to use them for strategic advantage. Understanding Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) in 2026 Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) is a critical metric for any B2B SaaS company, representing the total cost associated with acquiring a new customer. This includes marketing expenses, sales team salaries, and any other costs incurred in the customer acquisition process. Understanding CAC is essential as it directly impacts profitability and sustainability; if the cost to acquire a customer exceeds the revenue generated from that customer, the company risks financial instability. Recent trends indicate that the median CAC has remained steady at around $2.00 for every $1.00 of new Customer Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR). This ratio underscores the need for SaaS firms to optimize their acquisition strategies. Interestingly, the CAC payback period has also increased by 12.5% since 2022, suggesting that companies are spending longer to recoup their investments in acquiring customers. This shift emphasizes the importance of efficient resource allocation and effective lead nurturing to lower costs over time. To maintain or reduce CAC, B2B SaaS companies can implement several strategies. First, refining target customer profiles can lead to more qualified leads, thus enhancing conversion rates. Utilizing data analytics to monitor customer behavior allows companies to tailor their marketing tactics, improving engagement and reducing wasted ad spend. Additionally, developing a robust referral program can use existing customers to bring in new clients at a lower CAC. Moreover, integrating automated tools for inbound marketing can streamline customer interactions, ensuring leads are nurtured effectively while minimizing resources spent. By continuously analyzing and adapting acquisition strategies, small to mid-sized companies can maintain a healthy CAC that contributes positively to their overall financial performance and aligns with industry benchmarks. Keeping an eye on these trends and strategies allows businesses to make informed decisions that directly enhance their growth trajectory in an evolving market landscape. Analyzing Net Revenue Retention (NRR) for Sustained Growth Net Revenue Retention (NRR) is a critical metric that measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers over a specific period, typically a year. By factoring in upgrades, downgrades, and churn, NRR provides a comprehensive view of customer health and loyalty. A high NRR indicates that a company is not only retaining customers but also effectively expanding within its existing base, which is vital for sustainable growth. In the competitive landscape of B2B SaaS, understanding NRR can significantly influence strategic decision-making, as it ultimately impacts revenue forecasts and company valuations. According to forecasts for 2026, the benchmark NRR rate for B2B SaaS companies is expected to hover around 101%. This metric reflects a minor growth in retention capabilities, demonstrating a steady baseline that many firms can aspire to achieve. Companies striving for above-average performance may target NRR rates higher than this benchmark, which can contribute to their market advantage. Thus, focusing on NRR is not just beneficial; it’s essential for fostering long-term profitability and shareholder value. Improving NRR requires a proactive approach to customer success initiatives. By investing in customer onboarding, support, and engagement, SaaS businesses can enhance their customer experience, leading to lower churn rates and increased upselling opportunities. For instance, implementing regular check-ins, personalized training, and using feedback can create stronger relationships with customers. Businesses that prioritize these initiatives can expect not only to retain their existing clients but also to see increased expansion revenue from their current base.$1understanding and optimizing Net Revenue Retention is paramount for B2B SaaS companies aiming for sustained growth. By keeping a keen eye on this metric and focusing on customer success initiatives, businesses can ensure they remain competitive and financially robust in an ever-evolving market. Book a call The Role of Annual Contract Value (ACV) in SaaS Success Annual Contract Value (ACV) is a critical metric in the B2B SaaS landscape, representing the average yearly revenue generated from a customer contract. Understanding ACV helps businesses assess their financial health and is pivotal for strategic planning. Higher ACV indicates that a company has successfully positioned itself to offer comprehensive solutions that meet customer needs, making this metric essential for forecasting revenue growth and profitability. Benchmark ACV values can vary significantly across different market segments. For instance, enterprise-level SaaS companies may report ACVs exceeding $50,000, while small to mid-sized companies often see values around $10,000 to $20,000. Recognizing these benchmarks allows businesses to gauge their performance relative to competitors and understand market expectations. This contextual analysis can lead to more effective pricing strategies and targeted marketing efforts. One of the standout advantages of monitoring ACV is its ability to predict future revenue growth. By analyzing trends in ACV over time, businesses can identify patterns and make informed decisions about scaling operations. For example, if a company experiences a steady increase in ACV, it may suggest growing customer confidence and an opportunity for upselling or cross-selling additional services. Conversely, stagnation or decline in ACV could prompt a reassessment of customer engagement strategies and product offerings.$1a well-devised strategy around ACV not only contributes to immediate financial goals but also establishes a strong foundation for sustainable growth. Given that the median growth rate across B2B SaaS companies is around 26%, striving to optimize ACV should be a central focus for SaaS operators aiming to thrive in this competitive market. Understanding and using ACV effectively can empower small to mid-sized SaaS companies, providing them with crucial insights to enhance their market positioning and strategic initiatives. Breaking Down Expansion ARR and Growth Rates Expansion Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) is a vital metric for B2B SaaS companies, reflecting the revenue generated from existing customers through upsells, cross-sells, or expansions. Its significance lies not only in demonstrating customer satisfaction and loyalty but also in showcasing the potential for sustainable growth without heavily investing in new customer acquisition. For 2026, benchmarks suggest that a robust expansion ARR should ideally make up a substantial portion of Total New ARR, emphasizing the need for SaaS companies to focus on retaining and growing their existing customer base. The median growth rate across B2B SaaS companies is currently around 26%, indicating a strong upward trajectory for businesses that can effectively enhance their expansion ARR. Achieving and maintaining this growth requires a few strategic initiatives. First, companies should invest in customer success teams that proactively engage with existing clients to understand their evolving needs. This helps in identifying opportunities for upselling and ensures high customer satisfaction, which ultimately drives expansions. Another effective strategy involves implementing tailored marketing campaigns that highlight the additional features or services available to existing clients. These campaigns can increase awareness and utilization of products, significantly impacting overall revenue growth. Additionally, using data analytics allows companies to gain insights into customer behavior, leading to more informed decisions about when and how to expand services.$1focusing on Expansion ARR and enhancing growth rates is crucial for B2B SaaS companies aiming to thrive in the competitive landscape of 2026. Creating a granular understanding of customer needs and aligning business strategies accordingly will lead to greater customer retention and higher revenue. Comparing Benchmarks Across SaaS Market Segments When analyzing benchmarks across different SaaS market segments, it becomes clear that company size significantly affects key performance metrics. Small to mid-sized companies often operate with distinct benchmarks compared to large enterprises. For instance, while the median Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) may hover around $2.00 to acquire $1.00 of New Customer Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) for smaller firms, larger enterprises might see variances due to their established brand recognition and resources, impacting their growth strategies. These benchmarks hold essential implications for strategic planning. Small businesses typically need to rely more heavily on retention strategies, as they usually operate with tighter budgets and resources. In contrast, larger companies might prioritize scaling efforts to use existing market shares and brand loyalty. Understanding these differences allows leaders in small to mid-sized companies to make informed decisions, tailoring their strategies to optimize CAC and enhance customer retention. Consider a hypothetical scenario where a small SaaS startup, with a goal to achieve a 26% growth rate, focuses on optimally managing CAC through targeted marketing campaigns. Meanwhile, a large enterprise may implement more expansive strategies that emphasize cross-selling due to their ability to invest heavily in acquiring new customers. By recognizing these differences, firms can align their operational tactics to use benchmarks effectively, leading to more sustainable growth. Influence of Economic Factors on SaaS Benchmarks Economic factors play a crucial role in shaping B2B SaaS benchmarks, influencing everything from customer acquisition costs to revenue growth. Understanding trends such as inflation, technological advancements, and shifts in consumer behavior can help businesses identify key benchmarks relevant to their strategies. For example, fluctuations in economic conditions may drive up customer acquisition costs, which currently average $2.00 to garner $1.00 of new customer Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR). As economic landscapes evolve, businesses must adapt their strategies accordingly. This means revisiting pricing structures, evaluating customer retention efforts, and refining marketing campaigns to align with new benchmarks. A strategic response is essential; for instance, as the CAC payback period has seen a notable increase of 12.5% since 2022, companies might need to invest more in long-term relationships to sustain revenue inflow. Moreover, predicting future shifts is imperative for effective planning. Anticipating economic downturns can prepare SaaS companies to pivot quickly by prioritizing existing customer relationships and maximizing revenue from current clients. Growth strategies based on historical trends and anticipated market shifts can ensure that businesses remain nimble and responsive to the ever-changing economic climate, ultimately positioning them for sustainable success in the competitive SaaS landscape. From Benchmarks to Action: Strategic Recommendations Interpreting benchmark data is essential for strategic planning in the B2B SaaS landscape. Startups and small go-to-market (GTM) teams should focus on understanding how metrics like Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and Net Revenue Retention (NRR) relate to their specific business context. These insights can aid in identifying not only performance gaps but also growth opportunities. For instance, if the industry median CAC is $2 to acquire $1 of New Customer Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR), businesses can set realistic acquisition budgets and seek efficiencies in their marketing spend. Tailoring growth strategies to benchmark data allows teams to make informed adjustments. For example, if your NRR is below the average of 101%, it might signal the need for enhanced customer engagement strategies or upselling efforts to existing clients. Aligning product features and service offerings with established benchmarks can facilitate sustained growth and ensure that customer needs are being met effectively. Using benchmarks also provides a competitive advantage. By continuously monitoring these metrics against industry standards, businesses can quickly identify trends and pivot their strategies. This proactive approach fosters innovation and responsiveness to market demands, ultimately helping teams maintain a strong market position. Founders and GTM teams should take ownership of benchmark performance, employing them as vital tools in their strategic playbooks for effective growth management. title: What's New in April 2026: Flows Analytics, Custom Store Products, Web Checkouts, and AI in the dashboard. Plus a new iOS app.
summary: March gave you Flows. April is about making the platform deeper: analytics for Flows, products from any payment system, an AI agent in the dashboard, and new capabilities across web checkout. Oh, and we rebuilt the iOS app from scratch!
body_text: Flows Analytics: see exactly where users drop off and why Flows let you build multi-screen experiences right inside the Superwall editor — onboarding sequences, cancellation surveys, upsell paths, and feature walkthroughs — all with remote configuration and A/B testing. Now you get a full picture of how users move through your flow. Inside your experiment results, the new Flow Journey view brings: Drop-off by step — user counts and median time spent on each step. Branching view — Sankey-style diagrams that show how users split across conditional paths. Variant comparison — test entirely different flow structures against each other. The drop-off chart example Custom Store Products: sell from any payment system on any paywall Superwall now supports custom store products, so you can attach products from Stripe, your own backend, or any payment system to a Superwall paywall. You get the same functionality you already rely on with native store products — price variables, trial copy, eligibility checks, and A/B testing. That means you can place Stripe subscriptions alongside App Store subscriptions on the same paywall, sell lifetime access without StoreKit, and keep consistent experiment infrastructure across payment providers. Web Checkout: App2Web and one-time purchases App2Web. iOS paywalls can now open Stripe Checkout in Safari for U.S. storefront customers outside the app, following Apple's external purchase guidelines. Entitlements sync automatically as soon as the user returns. One-time purchases. Web checkout now supports Stripe one-time prices for lifetime access, credit packs, and consumables — no additional configuration required. AI Agent: ask anything about Superwall, right in the dashboard There's now an AI agent built into the dashboard, accessible from the bottom right corner. The agent has access to Superwall's documentation and SDK codebase, so you can ask how a feature works, how to set something up, or why a paywall is behaving a certain way — and get linked answers you can follow up on. AI Agent in your dashboard Superwall iOS App: every chart in your pocket, completely rebuilt Version 2 is a complete rewrite, putting over 20 dashboard charts on your phone. Adjust dates, apply filters and breakdowns, and scrub across data points with your finger. Export anything to JSON or Markdown. Transactions redesign. The overview and transaction history are now merged into one view, with detailed breakdowns including SDK events and purchase information. New home widgets. MRR, ARR, and a Recent Transaction widget that shows the latest purchases for your selected app. Revamped Superwall iOS App Apple Retention Messaging: control what users see when they cancel Superwall now integrates with Apple's Retention Messaging API, letting you configure the messages subscribers see when they start a cancellation through the App Store. You can show text messages, image messages, alternate product offers, and promotional offers. Set messages as defaults per product and locale, or configure them in real time based on the cancellation context. Apple invokes Superwall's callback URL, and Superwall returns the configured message. Retention messaging example Also shipped in April Priority Placements — a single-toggle campaign prioritization that enables preload optimization. Multipage paywall tracking — paywall_page_view events on every page within multi-page paywalls, for step-by-step drop-off analysis. SDK updates — iOS 4.14.2–4.15.1, Android 2.7.10–2.7.13, Flutter 2.4.12, Expo 1.0.9–1.1.1, with performance improvements and new features. Documentation updates — code block tabs, Vibe Coding guides, and intro offer eligibility clarifications.

title: Castle Biosciences Announces New York State Department of Health Approval of its AdvanceAD-Tx™ Test
summary: Approval expands access to Castle's precision medicine test designed to guide systemic treatment decision making in patients with…...
body_text: Approval expands access to Castle's precision medicine test designed to guide systemic treatment decision making in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis FRIENDSWOOD, Texas , July 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Castle Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: CSTL), a company improving health through innovative tests that guide patient care, today announced that it has received assay approval from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) for its AdvanceAD-Tx test. AdvanceAD-Tx is a non-invasive gene expression profile test designed to guide systemic therapy selection for patients aged 12 years and older with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD). "We are proud to announce the final approval of our AdvanceAD-Tx test by the NYSDOH's Clinical Laboratory Evaluation Program. This approval makes it easier than ever for patients in New York with moderate-to-severe AD to access a test which helps identify the class of systemic therapy to which they are most likely to respond based on the underlying biology of their disease," said Kristen Oelschlager, chief operating officer at Castle Biosciences. "New York State is the only U.S. jurisdiction that conducts a formal review of laboratory-developed tests before they can be offered to patients; this approval further demonstrates the level of quality and regulatory rigor we seek to achieve with each of our test offerings." With this approval, Castle has New York State approval for all tests within its dermatology and ophthalmology portfolios, its TissueCypher® test within gastroenterology and its clinical laboratories in Phoenix and Pittsburgh. "Too often, patients with AD spend months on therapies that do not adequately control their disease," said Matthew Goldberg, M.D., senior vice president, medical, at Castle Biosciences. "AdvanceAD-Tx was developed to provide clinicians with objective molecular insight that can help guide a more confident and personalized treatment decision from the start, with the goal of helping patients achieve meaningful relief from their symptoms sooner." AD is a chronic inflammatory skin disease that affects approximately 16.5 million adults and 9.6 million children in the United States. Despite a rapidly expanding treatment landscape, including T helper type 2 (Th2)-targeted biologics and Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor therapies, identifying the most appropriate systemic therapy for an individual patient remains a major clinical challenge. Patients frequently experience treatment switching and modification due to inadequate response, highlighting the need for molecular tools to guide therapy selection. AdvanceAD-Tx analyzes a patient's individual disease biology from a simple, non-invasive skin sample to classify them into one of two molecular profiles — a JAK Inhibitor Responder Profile or a Th2 Molecular Profile — providing clinicians with objective molecular insight to help guide systemic treatment selection. About AdvanceAD-Tx AdvanceAD-Tx is a non-invasive gene expression profile (GEP) test designed to guide systemic treatment decisions for patients aged 12 years and older with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD). Using RNA expression data from lesional skin scraping samples—no biopsy required—the test evaluates 487 genes across 12 inflammatory and cutaneous biology pathways to reveal the underlying immune biology driving an individual patient's disease. Results classify patients into one of two molecular profiles: a Janus kinase (JAK) Inhibitor Responder Profile or a T helper 2 (Th2) Molecular Profile. The prospective, clinical validation study showed that patients with a JAK Inhibitor Responder Profile given JAK inhibitor therapy experience significantly greater clinical benefit — including improved and faster skin clearance (EASI-90), greater likelihood of achieving no itch and remaining flare-free, and better quality of life by three months — compared to those treated with a Th2-targeted therapy.1 AdvanceAD-Tx provides clinicians with objective, molecular-based insights to help personalize systemic treatment decisions and improve care for patients. Learn more at https://castlebiosciences.com/tests/therapy-guidance/advancead-tx/overview . About Castle Biosciences Castle Biosciences (Nasdaq: CSTL) is a leading diagnostics company improving health through innovative tests that guide patient care. With a primary focus in dermatologic and gastroenterological disease, we develop personalized, clinically actionable solutions that help improve disease management and patient outcomes. We put people first—empowering patients and clinicians and informing care decisions through rigorous science and advanced molecular tests that support more confident treatment planning. To learn more, visit www.CastleBiosciences.com and connect with us on LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook and X . title: Cognyte Appoints Adam Philpott as Chief Revenue Officer to Lead Global Market Expansion
summary: The appointment reflects Cognyte's continuing investment in strengthening its commercial organization as the company advances its long-term growth strategy
body_text: HERZLIYA, Israel, July 22, 2026 – Cognyte Software Ltd . (NASDAQ: CGNT) (“Cognyte”), a global leader in AI-powered investigative analytics software, today announced the appointment of Adam Philpott as Chief Revenue Officer, effective August 1, 2026. Philpott will report to Chief Executive Officer Elad Sharon and join Cognyte’s executive management team. He succeeds Efi Nuri, who will retire after more than 30 years of service, following a smooth leadership transition. The appointment reflects Cognyte’s continuing investment in strengthening its commercial organization as the company advances its long-term growth strategy, deepens relationships with existing customers, and captures growing demand across global markets. Philpott brings more than 25 years of experience building and scaling go-to-market organizations across the U.S., EMEA and APAC into the public and enterprise markets. As Chief Revenue Officer at Trellix, formed by combining McAfee Enterprise and FireEye, he led a global commercial organization of more than 1,000 people and helped scale one of the industry’s largest enterprise cybersecurity businesses. He most recently served as Chief Executive Officer of Fingerprint Cards, a publicly traded biometrics company. Prior to these roles, he held senior sales leadership roles at McAfee and Cisco globally. Philpott is based in London. “As we enter our next phase of growth, we are strengthening our commercial leadership to build on the strong foundation we have established,” said Elad Sharon, Chief Executive Officer of Cognyte. “Adam brings a proven track record of scaling global businesses and executing disciplined go-to-market strategies worldwide, experience that positions him well to expand our market reach and capture the significant opportunities ahead. I also want to take this moment to recognize Efi Nuri for more than three decades of extraordinary contribution. Efi played a central role in building Cognyte’s global commercial organization, earning the trust of customers around the world, and establishing the strong foundation from which we are growing today. I am grateful for everything he has built and look forward to watching Adam and the team continue that momentum.” “Cognyte has established a leadership position in AI-powered investigative analytics by helping customers solve some of the world’s most complex security and investigative challenges,” said Adam Philpott. “I’m excited to join the company at this stage of its growth. My focus will be on strengthening commercial execution, expanding opportunities with customers and partners, and helping more organizations realize the value of Cognyte’s solutions.” “Serving Cognyte’s customers has been the privilege of my career,” said Efi Nuri. “I am incredibly proud of the relationships we have built, the talented global team we have developed, and everything we have accomplished together. I am confident Adam and the team will continue building on this momentum. I look forward to supporting a smooth transition and watching the company continue to grow.” About Cognyte Cognyte is a global leader in AI-powered investigative analytics solutions that empower customers with Actionable Intelligence for a Safer World®. Cognyte’s solutions enable law enforcement, national security and military intelligence agencies, as well as other organizations, to navigate an increasingly complex threat landscape. With offerings that leverage advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and analytics, Cognyte helps customers make sense of growing volumes of fragmented multi-source data to help identify, assess, and mitigate risks across dynamic environments, supporting informed, mission-critical investigations and operations. Hundreds of customers worldwide rely on Cognyte’s intelligence platform to uncover insights and reveal what matters, enabling confident decision-making in high-stakes environments. Learn more at www.cognyte.com .
